### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/lifecycle.mdx`  _(via os plugin publish (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/plugin/publish.ts))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx`  _(via os plugin publish (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/plugin/publish.ts))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via os plugin publish (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/plugin/publish.ts))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d770b1505e5b172c5a0cea2c22878067da2966b2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `005bd7b3809786f64fdd215561827c1790b0d532` — the merge of head `bd6d77e29bc0479703070e9407f5fca7795349c6` into base `d770b1505e5b172c5a0cea2c22878067da2966b2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 005bd7b3809786f64fdd215561827c1790b0d532 && git checkout 005bd7b3809786f64fdd215561827c1790b0d532
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d770b1505e5b172c5a0cea2c22878067da2966b2 bd6d77e29bc0479703070e9407f5fca7795349c6 && git checkout -B drift-repro d770b1505e5b172c5a0cea2c22878067da2966b2 && git merge --no-ff bd6d77e29bc0479703070e9407f5fca7795349c6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d770b1505e5b172c5a0cea2c22878067da2966b2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d770b1505e5b172c5a0cea2c22878067da2966b2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bd6d77e29bc0479703070e9407f5fca7795349c6`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cli/src/commands/plugin/publish.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/osplugin.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest-packaging-retirement.test.ts, packages/cli/test/plugin-publish.test.ts, docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/cli.json + packages/runtime/src/compiled-plugin-manifest.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest.zod.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/plugin/install.ts, packages/core/src/security/plugin-artifact-integrity.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/plugin/build.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/plugin/sign.ts

Face: `narrowing` (no path `hits`; the `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line on the PR body and the changeset decides it). On this face the floor is every diff path outside the prose faces, so the five non-prose paths above are all in scope; the one prose path, `.changeset/27810-plugin-publish-parses-compiled-manifest.md`, is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT` and is read here only for ②. Inputs: card #27810 (body + both comments, 6512268493 and 6513168362), PR #27910 (body, file list, net diff `origin/main` `d770b150`…`bd6d77e2`, merge-base = `origin/main`), and the head's check-runs. Cited code read on `origin/main` at `d770b150`, never the stale local checkout.

Check-runs on the head at 2026-10-30T03:37Z: every completed, non-skipped run is `success` — among them `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Test UI`, `Spec property liveness`, `Check PR Size`, `PR-body guards`. Still `in_progress` (pending, not a pass): `Test Core (1/8…8/8)`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check UI`. This PASS judges the diff; the landing still waits for those to conclude `success` (Multi-agent discipline §7), and a red among them re-opens this record.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept-set narrowing at `os plugin publish` — right, and exactly the card's ask.** `main` decoded the artifact's `objectstack.plugin.json` with a bare `JSON.parse` and checked only `id`/`version` presence and that `integrity` was an object. The head hands `readTarGz`'s entries to `readCompiledPluginManifest` (`packages/runtime/src/compiled-plugin-manifest.ts`, the helper PR #27791 gave `install.ts` line 302 and `installed-plugin-loader.ts` line 363) and refuses on `ok: false` before the signature read, the cloud-config read and both POSTs. The refused set is precisely what `ManifestSchema` (`strictObject`) refuses: a retired `packaging: 'manifest-deps'` (with its `enumWithRetiredValues` prescription), an unknown key, a missing `name`/`type`/`version`, a non-semver `version`, an `integrity` that is not a string→string record (`PluginIntegritySchema`), and `integrity: null` (which `main` let through to `verifyIntegrity`'s permissive null branch). Each of these is a tightening a publisher meets at their own terminal instead of at a consumer's install — the business reason on the card.
2. **No second copy of the rule — right.** Neither face file states a manifest rule. The hand-rolled malformed-`integrity` branch is deleted, and `verifyIntegrity(archiveFiles, manifest.integrity, …)` now takes the schema-typed `Record<string,string> | undefined`, matching the signature at `plugin-artifact-integrity.ts` line 75. `Artifact manifest is missing id or version.` survives and is reachable only through an empty `--manifest-id` (schema `version` is a required regex-matched string; `id` is required), as the body says.
3. **Payload of a valid publish unchanged — right.** `plugin_manifest` is the artifact's own JSON (re-decoded from the same entry), as on `main`; `scope`/`defaultDatasource` are not stamped in. The pin `uploads the manifest the artifact carries, as it carries it` holds this. `osplugin: base64`, `artifact_checksum`, the signature sidecar, auth precedence, visibility handling: untouched.
4. **`readOspluginManifest` sync → async, return type `Record<string, unknown>` → `ObjectStackManifestParsed` — an internal change, not a public-surface change.** `packages/cli/package.json` `exports` names `.`, `./console`, `./hook-body`; `src/index.ts` re-exports commands only; `utils/osplugin.ts` is on no entry. Its sole caller on `origin/main` is `packages/cli/test/plugin-publish.test.ts` (both pins updated to await). So `Clause-②: no` is right: nothing published widens. (Contrast PR #27791, which declared `yes (narrowing)` because it added the `readCompiledPluginManifest` export; this PR adds none.)
5. **Spec guard `EXCLUDED` entry — right and necessary.** The publish pins author `packaging: 'manifest-deps'` both in a spread literal and in two `it(...)` titles (double-quoted strings, not inline code, so `stripInlineCode` does not mask them); the walk's `AUTHORING` regex matches. The entry sits beside the install door's entry with the same one-line job statement, which is what the "⛔ NOT an allowlist file" rule asks of a structural exclusion. The retirement itself is not weakened: `PluginPackagingSchema.options` stays `['bundled']`.
6. **Fresh artifacts keep publishing.** `build.ts` line 361 compiles `{ ...manifest, main: 'dist/index.mjs', integrity }` from a manifest the build already parsed through `ManifestSchema`; `main` and `integrity` are declared keys, so a current `os plugin build` output passes the strict parse (the same fact #27791 relied on at install/boot).
7. **The PR body's "gate readings are in the `os-dev-report` comment on #27810"** — no such comment exists (the card has exactly two comments, triage and claim; the PR has docs-drift and the review claim). This record therefore relies on the head's check-runs alone, which is what the brief prescribes anyway. Not a tree defect; noted so the lane seat does not cite a comment that is not there.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/27810-plugin-publish-parses-compiled-manifest.md`: `'@objectstack/cli': minor`, `fix(cli)!`, **BREAKING** banner, one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`. The only package the diff moves is `@objectstack/cli` (`packages/spec` moves a test file only, `packages/runtime` is untouched) — right.
- Level per ruling A (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`): a declared kind (`narrowed`) ⇒ at least one moved package `minor`+ — `cli` is `minor`. ✓. `narrowed` beside a `(narrowing)` arm — no contradiction. ✓ `Check Changeset` is `success` on the head.
- `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` is the honest kind: a compiled-manifest value a publisher could carry through this door yesterday (`manifest-deps`, an unknown key, a null integrity map) is refused today — "a value refused or a requirement tightened is `narrowed`". It is also the kind the same family's PR #27791 declared for install and boot.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`: the diff narrows a published accept set (the publish door) and widens no public surface (①.4) — right. `(narrowing)` is the BREAKING signal; the banner and ADR-0087 disposition are present.
- ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is the right disposition: no key is added, removed, renamed or re-shaped; the remedy is "fix the source manifest as the refusal says, rebuild, re-sign" — a rebuild instruction, not a FROM → TO metadata migration, and no tombstone is owed (the `manifest-deps` tombstone already exists on `PluginPackagingSchema`). Same disposition as #27791, which the gate accepted.
- The PR body carries the `Skills-docs: none — REASON` line the `narrowed` kind owes.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Dev flag (1) — `plugin_manifest` uploaded verbatim, with a second decode of the entry.** Answered: **accepted, with one should-fix (④.1).** The read is right on substance: `ManifestSchema` stamps `defaultDatasource: 'default'` (`manifest.zod.ts` line 581) and `scope: 'project'` (line 636) at parse, so uploading `read.manifest` would change the declared manifest on every valid publish relative to `main`'s payload and relative to the bytes inside the signed artifact; that is not within the narrowing this PR declares (the card asks for a refusal, not a payload change), so keeping the artifact's own JSON is correct. The signature is over the whole artifact blob (`sign.ts` line 83, `signPayload(artifact, …)`), so the verbatim payload is not what the cloud's signature check hangs on — but the invariant "declared manifest == the manifest the blob carries" is still the sane one and the pin holds it. The second `JSON.parse` reads no rule and cannot disagree with the helper's decode (same bytes). What is weak is the shape, not the semantics: see ④.1.

**Dev flag (2) — `readOspluginManifest` async with a lazy `import('@objectstack/runtime')`.** Answered: **accepted.** `osplugin.ts` is imported by `build.ts`, `sign.ts`, `install.ts` and `publish.ts`; oclif's `pattern` strategy loads only the invoked command module, so a top-level import of the runtime root in the shared util would charge `os plugin build` and `os plugin sign` — which never read a compiled manifest back — a load `install` and `publish` already pay (both import `@objectstack/runtime` statically). The lazy import confines the cost to the one call that needs it; `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/spec` are `dependencies` of the CLI, the `./kernel` subpath the type import uses exists, and ESLint (`success` on the head) carries no restriction on `ImportExpression`. The function is internal (①.4), so async is a change its one caller absorbed in this diff. The ~1.2 s figure is the dev's measurement, not re-measured here; the design does not depend on the exact number.

No `open_questions` on the card. The card's own boundary ("no edit to the helper's own module unless the measurement demands it") was honoured: `compiled-plugin-manifest.ts` is untouched — which is also why ④.1 is a should-fix and not a defect of this PR.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/cli/src/commands/plugin/publish.ts` — holds.** Read against the helper's contract: `CompiledPluginManifestRead` is `{ ok: true; manifest }` or `{ ok: false; reason: 'unreadable' | 'invalid'; message; issues }`; the command maps `unreadable` to the pre-existing `Cannot read manifest from artifact:` sentence (the helper's message for a missing entry is `objectstack.plugin.json not found`, so the old absent-manifest wording is preserved) and `invalid` to one `• path: message` line per issue plus the rebuild/re-sign remedy, then `this.exit(1)`. The helper never throws (it catches internally), so leaving it outside the `readTarGz` try-block is correct. Ordering is as the card asks: the refusal precedes the integrity preflight, the `.sig` read, `tryReadCloudConfig` and both `postJson` calls; the pins count `fetch` at 0. Scenario tried: an artifact whose manifest is valid but whose `integrity` digests are stale — still refused by the integrity preflight, unchanged. Artifact with no `integrity` map — still a permissive skip (`.optional()`), unchanged. `--manifest-id` override still wins over `manifest.id`. Zod issue order for the drifted pin (`name` before `integrity`) follows `strictObject` key order (line 674 before line 1106), so the regex pin is deterministic.
  1. **should-fix (follow-up, not blocking):** the verbatim payload is produced by `JSON.parse(Buffer.from(archiveFiles.find((f) => f.path === MANIFEST_FILENAME)!.data)…)` — a non-null assertion and a second decode, guaranteed today only because `MANIFEST_FILENAME` (cli) and `COMPILED_PLUGIN_MANIFEST_FILE` (runtime) are two constants spelling the same string, and the helper found the entry. If they ever drift, the `!` turns a refusal into a TypeError. The sustainable shape is for `readCompiledPluginManifest` to hand back the raw document it already decoded (or the entry it found) so the door decodes once and asserts nothing; that edit was outside this card's file surface by dispatch, so it is a one-line follow-up card against `packages/runtime/src/compiled-plugin-manifest.ts`, not a FAIL here.

**`packages/cli/src/utils/osplugin.ts` — holds.** `readOspluginManifest` now returns the helper's parsed manifest and throws `read.message` for both `unreadable` and `invalid`; the `/not found/` pin and the two new prescription pins read that message. The module stays free of oclif and filesystem, as its header promises. Tried to break it: a caller awaiting the old sync return — none exists outside the updated test (①.4). The lazy import under tsup/vitest resolves the workspace package the same way `install.ts`'s static import does.

**`packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest-packaging-retirement.test.ts` — holds.** One `EXCLUDED` entry, placed beside the install door's entry, with a one-line job statement in the same voice. The walk's anti-vacuity floors (`visited > 1000`, `mentioning > 3`) are unaffected by excluding one more file. The exclusion covers only `packages/cli/test/plugin-publish.test.ts`; `publish.ts` and `osplugin.ts` themselves spell the value only in prose comments and inline code (`` `packaging: 'manifest-deps'` ``), which `stripInlineCode` removes — so the production files stay under the walk, as they should.

**`packages/cli/test/plugin-publish.test.ts` — holds.** Five new pins and two updated: the two door refusals count `fetch` calls (0) and match the prescription on a `•` line; the verbatim-payload pin is `toEqual(manifest)` plus two `not.toHaveProperty` on the stamped defaults, so it reds if the parsed value is ever uploaded; the `readOspluginManifest` pins cover `unreadable` and both `invalid` shapes. The fixture manifest (`id`, `name`, `version`, `type`, `runtime`, `packaging: 'bundled'`, `main`, `permissions`, `integrity`) is a manifest `ManifestSchema` accepts, so the happy path is real, not vacuous.

**`docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/cli.json` — holds.** Item `cli.plugin-manifest-build-contract` revision 6 → 7: the compiled-manifest clause and its verify step now name the schema refusal sentence that `publish.ts` prints and the `version: …` issue a version-less manifest yields; the `publish.ts#version` source row names `readCompiledPluginManifest` and the empty `--manifest-id` refusal; a history entry with `ref: "#27810"` follows the revision-6 entry's shape. Every sentence in it is true of the head.

**Verdict on the narrowing itself, against the published spec on `main`:** it takes no declared capability away at the consumer — it makes `ManifestSchema`'s own refusal real at the third and last door that reads a compiled manifest, so the three doors (`publish`, `install`, boot) now agree, and nothing a valid `os plugin build` produces is refused. That is Prime Directive #12 ("reject it at authoring/publish so the error surfaces loudly") done the way #10 asks.

## 维护者速读
- 改了什么：`os plugin publish` 用安装和启动已在用的 `readCompiledPluginManifest` 按 `ManifestSchema` 校验 `.osplugin` 的编译清单，不合格就在任何网络请求前拒绝并给处方。
- 为什么改：以前发布只做 `JSON.parse`，带已退役键（如 `packaging: 'manifest-deps'`）的包能传上市场，要到用户安装时才被拒（#27810）。
- 风险与回滚：收窄（`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`）：不合 schema 的清单从此发不出去；合法包照常发布，上传的 `plugin_manifest` 仍是包内原样 JSON。回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看：`publish.ts` 第 2 步，再看 `osplugin.ts` 的 `readOspluginManifest`。
- 两分钟验证：`plugin-publish.test.ts` 新增 5 例；还原两处源码后 4 例拒绝钉子变红。
- 需要你做的：无（非受管；契约复审 PASS 6514352615；席位按本任落地授权落地）。

席位意见：ACCEPT。

## 席位核对

Head-sha: `bd6d77e29bc0479703070e9407f5fca7795349c6`

- **Shape:** the publish door validates the compiled manifest through `readCompiledPluginManifest` (`@objectstack/runtime`, the helper #27791 gave install and boot) before the signature read, the cloud-config read and both POSTs, and refuses with the schema's issue lines; the hand-rolled integrity check gives way to the schema-typed `manifest.integrity`; the uploaded `plugin_manifest` stays the artifact's own JSON (the parsed value would stamp `scope` / `defaultDatasource`). `readOspluginManifest` goes through the same helper, now async with a lazy runtime import (internal; sole caller the updated test). Changeset `@objectstack/cli` minor, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, ADR-0087 disposition carried. `check-governed-merges --pr 27910`: NOT governed, 190 changed lines.
- **Premise measured:** 5 new pins + 2 updated, 12/12; ablation (publish.ts + osplugin.ts from `main`) turns the 4 refusal pins red, the parsed-value upload turns the verbatim pin red; CLI unit layer 351 files / 5090 tests; `dispatch-gates --ran` 87 derived, 87 run, all exit 0 after a whole-tree build (dev report 6514552840 on #27810).
- **Dogfood battery:** 4 reds on the PR's base, all `main`'s and fixed on `main` by #27878 and #27873; on a local unpushed merge of current `main` the three red files pass 60/60. Not this diff.
- **Gate check-runs on the head:** 50 runs, 40 success, 10 skipped, 0 failure/pending; `mergeable_state` clean.
- **Contract review:** PASS, record 6514352615 on this head, no must-fix; its one should-fix (the second manifest decode keyed by a separately spelled filename) is outside this card's surface and filed as #27914.
- **Accepted deviations:** the surface took one `EXCLUDED` entry in `packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest-packaging-retirement.test.ts` (test-only) and the `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/cli.json` rows, both by claim amendment before the edit; `readOspluginManifest` became async.
- **Landing:** under the maintainer's landing grant for this seat term (seat 4 thread, 2026-10-29 22:04Z): `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` through the relay.
